Long duration (1.454x central) and star_density_penalty 38.75; stellar RADIUS measurement and radial velocity mass limit would test grazing vs planet density.
dossier.public_summary: This is a 3.6 Earth-radius dip repeating every 13.8 days on a nearby M dwarf, seen in two sectors with no difference image showing a neighbor and no odd-even or strong secondary eclipse. The star is spotted and active, which causes light-curve wobble and modest depth scatter, but the size, flat bottom, and lack of binary signs make a planet the best explanation. Precise photometry and mass measurement are still needed to confirm.

reasons.why: Sub-Neptune size well below stellar/brown-dwarf regime positively favors planet; flat bottom shape.v_sigma -1.699 also planet-like.
No significant odd/even difference and secondary below SNR 5 threshold; best_brightening_snr 3.731 outruns it, consistent with noise, disfavoring an eclipsing binary at half period or 2x period.

No star within one pixel (21 arcsec) can cause this depth with <=25% eclipse; closest that could is 36.8 arcsec away needing 0.2621 eclipse, so a background-blend NEB is unlikely despite inconclusive centroid.

Depth variation is sector-source dependent and consistent with two apertures over a spotted M dwarf, not intrinsic change; long observed duration relative to central 2.75 h and high impact parameter star density penalty 38.75 are expected for spot-crossing/grazing geometry on an M0.5 dwarf (Teff 3548, Rad 0.5006, VARIABLE), which the scorer weights against but the size and lack of binary signs outweigh.
reasons.value: sector_depths_by_source.verdict steady p_constant 0.04903 (QLP 4829 ppm, SPOC 3652 ppm same source steady), duration.ratio 1.454 fit_b 0.8713

reasons.why: Individual transit depths scatter more than formal errors and star shows ~7.4 d spot variability with signal at 1.867x rotation, explaining excess scatter and apparent duration/star-density mismatch via spots/systematics; not evidence for separate astrophysical eclipses.
